full_judgment:
2. It has been asserted in the revisional application that the opposite party Nos.1 and 2 as pre-emptor initiated Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2004 before the Assistant Judge, Jokigonj, Sylhet under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which has been further re-numbered as Pre-emption Case No. 17 of 2007. 

 4. The pre-emptee No.1, petitioner, before this Court, contested the said pre-emption case by filing written objection denying all the material allegations made in the pre-emption application contending inter alia that the pre- emptor had knowledge about the transfer from the initiation and since after the development work made by the purchase-pre-emptee the value of the case land has been increased the pre-emptor filed the case on the false statement. The preemptors are not co-sharer of owners of the contiguous land. There is a intervening road in between the land owned by the pre-emptors and the transferred land. Therefore, the pre-emptors had no right to pre-empt the case land, and hence the present case for pre-emption is liable to be rejected with cost. 

 15. In substantiating the said argument the learned Advocate Barrister AKM Nazrul Islam further drawn the attention of this Court to the evidence of the OPW 1 and argued that the OPW 1 has categorically stated that the alleged road is a private road established on the land of the pre-emptors and, as such, the path-way as has been mentioned by the Advocate Commissioner as a road for the public, being a wrong committed by the Advocate Commissioner was correctly disagreed by the Courts below and, as such, no question of committing error occasioning failure of justice comes at all. 

 16. The learned Advocate Mr. AKM Nazrul Islam further argued that the Map of the Mouza Kadam Rasul has clearly showed that no road was established by any Government authority in between Plot No. 408, the transferred land, and the Plot No. 407, owned by the pre-emptor and the admitted pathway in between this two plot has been created by the pre-emptor and the title of that portion of the plot, as used as pathway, remains with the pre-emptor and, as such, the contiguity in between these plot of 407 and 408 has never been destroyed. Therefore, the right of pre-emption rendered, under the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, to a contiguous land holder is available to the pre-emptor which the Courts below has correctly found and accordingly passed order for preemption which is not liable to be interfered with by this Court.
